summary.en: Find an owning link, update list positions and remove nodes without losing the chain.
summary.bn: নোডের মালিক লিংক খুঁজে position-এ কাজ করো, আর চেইন ঠিক রেখে নোড মুছো।

notes: These implementations use C17. Compound literals and declarations in loop headers date from C99; C17 does not add automatic memory management.

examples.title: Delete the first matching value
examples.explanationHtml: The pointer-to-pointer identifies the field that owns the matching node. Redirecting that field works for the head and for interior nodes.

examples.title: Insert and delete by position
examples.explanationHtml: Position zero accepts insertion even when the list is empty. Deleting position one removes the old head when it exists.

examples.title: Find an index and count nodes
examples.explanationHtml: The index counts links from head. Continuing after the first match is necessary because this example also needs the total node count.

examples.title: Release every node and clear the owner
examples.explanationHtml: destroy saves next before freeing each node. The caller clears head because passing head by value cannot clear the caller’s pointer.

practice.title: Insert at a zero-based position
practice.statementHtml: Read n (0..16), then n values (-99..99). Read position (0..16) and value (-99..99); print Inserted: success and List:.
hints: Stop at the owner field for the insertion gap.

practice.title: Delete by position
practice.statementHtml: Read n (0..16), then n values (-99..99). Read a position, print Removed: success and the remaining List:.
hints: An empty owner field means no node can be removed.

practice.title: Erase every matching node
practice.statementHtml: Read n (0..16), then n values (-99..99). Read target, repeatedly erase its first occurrence, and print Removed: count and List:.
hints: Repeated search is correct, though a single pass can be faster.

practice.title: Delete alternating positions
practice.statementHtml: Read n (0..16), then n values (-99..99). Remove original indices 1,3,5,... and print List:.
hints: After removing a successor, advance to the next retained node.

quiz.prompt: What does the owner pointer identify during erase_value?
options: The pointer field that leads to the current node
quiz.explanation: Starting at &head and advancing to a next field lets the same update remove head or an interior node.

quiz.prompt: Which position is invalid for deletion from a size-three list?
quiz.explanation: Live positions are zero through two. Position three is an insertion gap but contains no node to delete.

quiz.prompt: What should deleting an absent value do?
options: Report failure and preserve the chain
quiz.explanation: An absent target provides no victim. The list and its ownership remain unchanged.

options: All deletions require a new allocation
The live chain must retain the successor address
quiz.explanation: Saving or assigning the successor while victim is alive avoids reading released storage.

quiz.prompt: What is worst-case time for search and count on n nodes?
quiz.explanation: Without an index or stored count, the code may need to visit the complete chain.

quiz.prompt: If a separate tail is maintained, deleting the only node must do what?
options: Leave tail pointing to the freed node
Set both head and tail to NULL
Point tail to an arbitrary neighbor
quiz.explanation: The singleton is both endpoints. A dangling tail would make the next append unsafe.

quiz.prompt: How many allocations does erase_at normally need?
quiz.explanation: Deletion releases an existing node. Walking to its owner does not require allocating anything.

quiz.prompt: After bypassing the middle node, which value follows head?
quiz.explanation: a.next is reassigned to b.next, which identifies c. The following value is therefore 36.

quiz.prompt: Which value becomes head when the original first node is bypassed?
quiz.explanation: head takes a.next, which identifies b. The new first value is 85; no payload value was copied.

quiz.prompt: How many nodes remain when two of five are removed?
quiz.explanation: Five original nodes minus two removed nodes leaves three. This count model does not itself release any nodes.

quiz.prompt: After removing a matching node during a one-pass filter, where should the owner cursor stay?
options: At the removed node’s next field
At the address of the freed allocation
quiz.explanation: The same owner now leads to the successor, which still needs inspection. The removed node’s fields are dead.

quiz.prompt: Why does insertion at size succeed while deletion at size fails?
options: Positions are one-based only for delete
The final gap exists but contains no live node
quiz.explanation: Insertion names a boundary gap. Deletion names an existing element at an index strictly below size.

keyPoints.en: A pointer-to-pointer can identify either head or an interior next field.
keyPoints.bn: পয়েন্টারের পয়েন্টার দিয়ে head বা ভেতরের next ঘর ধরা যায়।

keyPoints.en: Insertion accepts the gap after the final node as a valid position.
keyPoints.bn: শেষ নোডের পরের ফাঁকেও position দিয়ে insert করা যায়।

keyPoints.en: Deletion redirects the owner before freeing the removed node.
keyPoints.bn: Delete করতে আগে মালিক লিংক ঘোরাও, তারপর বাদ দেওয়া নোড free করো।

keyPoints.en: Search returns the first matching position when duplicates are allowed.
keyPoints.bn: একই মান একাধিকবার থাকলে সার্চ প্রথম মেলা position দিতে পারে।

keyPoints.en: Whole-list destruction saves each successor before releasing its owner node.
keyPoints.bn: পুরো লিস্ট ছাড়ার সময় প্রতিবার free-এর আগে পরের নোড রেখে দাও।

examQuestions.question: Delete the first 85 from [72,85,85,91] and show the owner field change.
examQuestions.answerHtml: The owner is the next field in node 72. It changes from the first 85 node to the second 85 node. Free only the first match. The result is [72,85,91].

examQuestions.question: Write the core deletion through Node **link when *link is a valid victim.
examQuestions.answerHtml:
Node *victim = *link;
*link = victim->next;
free(victim);

For head deletion link is &head. For an interior node it is the predecessor’s next field. Check *link before entering these steps.

examQuestions.question: List edge cases for insertion and deletion by position.
examQuestions.answerHtml: Empty insertion at zero succeeds if allocation succeeds; larger positions fail. Empty deletion fails. A singleton supports deletion at zero. Negative positions fail. Insertion at size appends; deletion at size fails. A maintained tail must be repaired when its node is removed.

examQuestions.question: Repeatedly erase one target by searching from head. Give a worst-case cost and a faster approach.
examQuestions.answerHtml: Repeated searches can scan long prefixes for many deletions, giving O(n squared) worst-case time. A single owner-pointer traversal bypasses matching nodes as it goes, giving O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
